omissions.element: How many disabled children are out of school, and why
omissions.reason: Step 1 fails. The finding explains why children with disabilities fall behind: [S001@7978-8016] different impairment types. That is a barrier description, which the SCOPE entry 'How many disabled children are out of school, and why' excludes as context that does not show whether interventions work. Step 2: the draft already states that this group falls behind in enrolment, retention and completion. It also already states the review's call for a twin-track, more systemic approach. So the finding would add nothing on whether programmes work or which work best.

Step 1: The finding concerns which kinds of intervention work best, which is part of THE QUESTION, and no SCOPE exclusion applies. Step 2: The draft already makes the same point. It says the review 'does not establish a single best kind of programme' and that the sources 'do not support ranking one kind of programme as the best'. It also gives the authors' conclusion that a twin-track approach is needed, which implies no single intervention suffices. Adding 'no magic bullet' would not change the answer for the reader. Its verbatim wording also says 'health outcomes', which does not match the review's education focus, so adding it could mislead.
